findings.text: Pool size attributes share common show and store helpers. Show reports a global or per-node pool count. Store parses an unsigned decimal count and forwards a mempolicy-obedience flag plus resolved state and node to a common resize helper. Plain and mempolicy variants differ only in that flag.

Overcommit limit attribute has a global show and a guarded store. Store rejects gigantic states without runtime support and rejects non-numeric input, otherwise replaces the stored overcommit allowance and reports the full input length.

Free, reserved, and surplus counters are read-only status attributes. Free and surplus honor the object node scope, selecting global versus per-node storage; reserved always reports the global reservation counter.

Demote attribute consumes a requested demote count. It scopes allowed nodes to one node when the object is per-node, else to all memory nodes, then repeatedly demotes from free pages while excluding reserved pages until the request is exhausted or no demotable pages remain.

Demote size attribute reports current target size in kilobytes and accepts a size string. Store resolves the requested size to a huge-page state and validates that its order is at least huge-page minimum and strictly below the owning state order before updating the target.

Node scope is derived from the sysfs object. A no-node marker selects aggregate pool state; any other node selects the same counter indexed for that node. Overcommit, reservation, and demote size ignore node scope and always use global state.

Demote operation nests a per-state resize mutex outside the global huge-page spin lock. The per-iteration pool helper may drop the spin lock, so available free-minus-reserved capacity is recomputed under the lock on every loop iteration.

Overcommit updates are serialized by an interrupt-safe global huge-page spin lock. Demote target updates are serialized by the owning state resize mutex. Vmemmap table splitting serializes installation with the initial address space table lock and only installs when the target remains a leaf.

Per-node huge-page sysfs bookkeeping holds one parent object for the node plus one child object per huge-page state size, stored in a fixed array indexed by state and instantiated once per possible node.

Global huge-page attribute set contains pool size, overcommit, free, reserved, surplus, and on NUMA an additional mempolicy pool attribute. Demote group contains demote size and demote. Per-node group contains only pool size, free, and surplus.
A one-time initialization flag records whether huge-page sysfs setup completed and is marked read-only after init.

Vmemmap remap walk carries a per-entry remap callback, a count of visited entries, head and tail reuse pages, a list collecting replaced backing pages, and flags controlling whether table split and entry remap each skip kernel range TLB flushing.

Vmemmap table preparation walks page-table levels with two callbacks. Table-level callback splits large mappings into page tables when backing exists and otherwise stops; entry-level callback invokes the configured remap operation and advances the visited count. Absence of a remap callback means split-only traversal.

Vmemmap optimization remaps the first visited entry to a writable reused head page and later entries to a shared read-only tail page, queuing displaced backing pages. Restore leaves non-tail mappings alone, otherwise recycles a queued page, copies current contents into it, and reinstalls it writable. Ordering barriers separate content stores from table installation.

Boot-time vmemmap optimization is enabled only when a global toggle is set, the boot page state is optimizable, and both its physical address and size are aligned to memory section size and to the address range covered by one vmemmap table entry.

Early boot initialization iterates boot huge pages on a node, skips ineligible pages, populates a reduced vmemmap over the needed range, accounts reserved pages, marks each covered section as vmemmap preinitialized, and flags the boot page as optimized. Population failure halts boot.

Vmemmap preparation refuses self-hosted hotplug vmemmap on first encounter. Table split allocates a new table and frees it if the target is no longer a leaf. Non-reserved large backing is split before installing page tables so members remain independently releasable.

Reserved vmemmap area per optimizable huge page is one base page; reserved page count is that byte size divided by descriptor size. The implementation asserts at build time that used subpage count fits within the reserve.

Vmemmap optimization exposes a boolean control named hugetlb_optimize_vmemmap under vm with read-write owner and read-only group and other access. A boot parameter of the same feature parses a boolean into the same toggle. Registration occurs only if some huge-page state is optimizable.
Diagnostic messages from the vmemmap optimization component carry a HugeTLB log prefix.

Hardware-poison injection accepts a page frame number, requires administrative privilege and a valid frame, and without filtering enabled directly invokes simulated memory failure. With filtering enabled it drains state, requires a reclaimable, huge, or free-buddy target, applies an allow-list check, and treats filter failure or unsupported result as a silent success.
Poison filter chain is bypassed entirely when disabled. When enabled it successively requires device match, page-flag match, and cgroup or task match; any stage failure rejects the page.

Filter defaults are disabled with wildcard device identifiers, empty flag mask, and zero cgroup selector. Device filtering passes when both identifiers are wildcards, otherwise requires a mapped file host and matching major and minor unless individually wildcarded. Flag filtering passes with empty mask, otherwise requires masked stable flags to equal the configured value.
Cgroup task filtering passes when the configured selector is zero, otherwise requires the page cgroup identifier to equal it. An alternate build provides an unconditional pass for task filtering.
Folio draining helper does nothing for huge or slab folios and otherwise drains all per-CPU reclaim lists.

Memory failure handling first panics if recovery is disabled, marks hardware-originated failures, then dispatches non-online frames to architecture, non-page, device-map, or outside-control paths. Online huge pages go to a huge-page path; other pages that are already poisoned return poisoned or terminate the accessor when action is required.

Zero-count poisoned frames are not reference-counted. Free buddy frames are removed from the allocator under a one-retry race protocol; other zero-count frames are reported as ignored high-order kernel pages. Unhandlable stable kernel pages and transient allocator races are reported as ignored without recovery.

Memory failure serializes under a dedicated failure mutex from entry until the selected terminal path. Large folio handling locks the folio to test the user poison filter, clears poison and drops the reference on filter rejection, otherwise marks the folio poisoned and attempts a split before later handling.
